data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest reclamation protocol is a content-addressed seal-before-grant dependency: workspace reclamation for a deterministic problem ID must be gated on the visibility of a durable, content-addressed seal of all completed evidence in a logically separate, higher-durability ledger, and the workspace itself must carry no authority to overwrite evidence without this external seal proof.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The seal ledger suffers correlated failure with the workspace host, breaking visibility","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The protocol optimistically grants workspace before seal visibility due to latency pressure","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Content-addressed collision resistance is practically or theoretically compromised","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Before any workspace is reclaimed, the protocol queries a durable seal ledger by problem ID. If a content-addressed evidence hash exists under that problem ID, reclamation proceeds only after cryptographic verification of the hash. The process emits heartbeats, but these merely manage liveness, not displacement authority. The durable record must contain: (1) the problem-workspace binding, (2) the content-addressed evidence hash in the seal ledger, and (3) a signed checkpoint of the seal ledger prefix up to that hash. This makes displacement contingent on data availability rather than process state.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
